offence_severity: Minimum: 10 years, Maximum: Life imprisonment (Section 302 IPC)
physical_harm: Injury on the neck leading to death
number_of_offences: Charged with 2 offences; 1 upheld (Section 302 IPC) and 1 upheld (Sections 25/27 Arms Act)
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the Appellant shot the deceased during a marriage ceremony with a country-made pistol, resulting in a fatal injury to the deceased's neck. The Appellant confessed to his guilt in his statement under Section 161 CrPC. The FIR and the post-mortem report were also accepted as key evidence.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as hostile, with many of them turning against the prosecution during cross-examination. The credibility of the witnesses was undermined as they provided conflicting accounts and were found to be based on hearsay.
trial_duration: FIR registered on 17.03.2016, trial judgment dated 23.02.2018, High Court decision dated 04.04.2019, Supreme Court decision dated 11 March 2024
legal_representation: Sanjay Kumar Dubey, Shuchi Singh, Rakesh Kumar Tewari, Mr./Ms. Krishna Kant Dubey, Vivek Kumar Pandey, Ujjawal Kr. Dubey, Aman, Advs. for the Appellant; Ardhendumauli Kumar Prasad, Sr. A.A.G., Vishnu Shankar Jain, Aayush Mishra, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered under s.302 IPC and s.25, 27 Arms Act, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court convicted under s.302 IPC; High Court upheld the conviction; Supreme Court set aside s.302 conviction, convicted under s.304 Part II IPC
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the Appellant shot the deceased during a marriage ceremony, resulting in his demise, and that the Appellant was guilty of the offence under Section 302 IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no previous enmity between the deceased and the Appellant, no intention to cause death, and that the act of celebratory firing during a marriage ceremony should not be construed as an act so imminently dangerous to cause death.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that an act is punishable under Section 304 Part II IPC if it is done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death, even if there is no intention to cause death.
precedent_relied_upon: Kunwar Pal Singh v. State of Uttarakhand, (2014) 12 SCC 434; Bhagwan Singh v. State of Uttarakhand, (2020) 14 SCC 184
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the Appellant's act of celebratory firing in a crowded place without taking safety measures led to the death of the deceased, and the Appellant was found guilty of culpable homicide under Section 304 Part II IPC.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court considered the absence of previous enmity, the lack of intention to cause death, and the fact that the Appellant had already undergone approximately 8 years of incarceration.
other_sentence_order: The conviction and sentence under Sections 25 & 27 of the Arms Act remain unaltered. The Appellant is to be released forthwith if not required in any other case.
